brief.question: Can output-Jacobian-selected sparse residual coefficients improve logit fidelity at a matched total padded serialized-bit budget while bounding task degradation in frozen GNN-to-SNN compression?
brief.answer: On the reported test split, rank-128 SVD transport with a 2% output-Jacobian-selected sparse residual budget reduced the ratio of three-seed mean split-specific logit MSE by 26.23%, 33.99%, and 25.83% versus the strongest evaluated matched-budget control on Cora, Chameleon, and Squirrel; maximum three-seed-mean task degradation was 1.86 pp and maximum seed-level degradation was 2.85 pp.
brief.audience: Graph-compression and neuromorphic-conversion researchers evaluating fidelity/resource trade-offs of frozen ANN/GNN-to-SNN conversion.
brief.domain_bridge: Repeated high-dimensional A X messages dominate transport; retain an operator-aligned rank-128 basis and spend a 2% sparse residual budget on coefficients with high output-Jacobian sensitivity; matched-budget tests show lower logit MSE with bounded task loss.

main: logit-MSE improvement at matched padded bits

terminology.sparse residual coefficients: selected exact message residual values with explicit indices; not temporal spikes
terminology.matched padded bits: identical total_padded_bits within a dataset/seed/rank/budget comparison, allowing different payload lengths
terminology.held-out confirmation: test run after validation-exposed reframing, not preregistered independent replication

paragraph_plan.point: Low-rank graph-message transport can preserve the wrong output-sensitive directions under a fixed serialization budget.
Output-Jacobian squared sensitivity selects sparse residual coefficients after SVD transport under an exact padded-bit ledger.
The held-out test run confirms logit-MSE reductions on all three graphs at matched total padded serialized-bit budget.
Hidden-MSE and budget-grid sensitivity show that output-sensitive fidelity improves across evaluated settings.
Task degradation remains bounded, but task superiority is not established; warmed cost is modest in the measured 1% setting.
The evidence supports a local fidelity/resource contribution with explicit static-GCN, conversion, and measurement limits.
Output-Jacobian residual allocation improves logit fidelity within the tested frozen-GCN scope while bounding observed task loss.

qualification_placement.repeat_when: any statement of generality, novelty, energy, or event semantics

section_jobs.Introduction: Open from output-sensitive information loss in compressed graph messages; state the bounded logit-fidelity question and contribution.
section_jobs.Methods: Define SVD transport, exact padded-bit ledger, output-Jacobian score, sparse coefficient encoding, rate-coded conversion and evaluation scope.
section_jobs.Experiments and Results: Report matched-budget logit MSE, bounded task loss, prior-art adaptations and warmed cost without table-cell narration.
section_jobs.Discussion: Interpret fidelity gains and task trade-offs; distinguish observed results from mechanism hypotheses; state limits.
section_jobs.Conclusion: Answer the question with the three-graph result and no new promise.

facts.statement: At rank 128 and a 2% sparse residual budget on the reported test split, output-Jacobian selection reduced the ratio of three-seed mean split-specific logit MSE versus the strongest evaluated matched-budget control by 26.23% on Cora, 33.99% on Chameleon, and 25.83% on Squirrel; all nine dataset-seed comparisons improved.
facts.model: frozen two-layer hidden-16 GCN checkpoint seeds 0/1/2
facts.condition: SVD rank 128 plus 2% output-Jacobian-selected sparse residual coefficients
facts.aggregation: ratio of three-seed mean per dataset
facts.uncertainty: all nine dataset-seed paired comparisons positive; no formal CI claimed
facts.measurement_scope: reported test split; validation-exposed reframing preceded the run

facts.statement: The maximum three-seed-mean degradation across T=2/4 accuracy and teacher agreement was 1.86 percentage points; the largest seed-level degradation was 2.85 percentage points.
facts.model: frozen two-layer hidden-16 GCN checkpoint seeds 0/1/2
facts.metric: task degradation relative to strongest control

facts.statement: All compared rank-128/2% methods used identical total padded serialized bits within each dataset, although payload lengths and coefficient counts could differ.
Across nine dataset-seed pairs, paired p95 full-pipeline runtime ratios versus SVD-only ranged from 1.020 to 1.124, and peak CUDA allocation was 218.23 MB.
facts.model: RTX3060 warmed benchmark with three warmups and seven measured repeats
facts.aggregation: p95 range across dataset-seed pairs; maximum memory
facts.uncertainty: timing variance retained in raw repeats

facts.statement: The focal setting and logit-fidelity reframing were fixed after validation exposure and before the test run; the test run is held-out confirmation, not preregistered or independent replication. Sparse residual coefficients are not temporal SNN events, and no energy or broad GNN-generality claim is supported.
facts.attribution: run contract and independent pre-draft review

facts.statement: At rank 128 and the 2% residual budget, hidden-state MSE fell by 16.88%, 12.86%, and 10.63% relative to the strongest matched-budget control on Cora, Chameleon, and Squirrel.
facts.model: frozen two-layer hidden-16 GCN checkpoint seeds 0/1/2
facts.condition: SVD rank 128 plus 2% output-Jacobian-selected sparse residual coefficients
facts.uncertainty: descriptive sensitivity result; no formal CI claimed

facts.statement: Across the evaluated 0.5%, 1%, and 2% residual budgets and three graphs, logit MSE was below the strongest corresponding control in all nine dataset-budget cells, with reductions from 2.98% to 30.40%.
facts.model: frozen two-layer hidden-16 GCN checkpoint seeds 0/1/2
facts.condition: SVD rank 128 with output-Jacobian-selected sparse residuals
facts.metric: logit MSE relative reduction over matched-budget grid
facts.uncertainty: validation-grid sensitivity; focal 2% setting later received held-out confirmation

facts.statement: At rank 128 and 2%, the proposed selector reduced three-seed mean logit MSE relative to our matched-budget A2Q-style adaptation by 28.93%, 36.19%, and 35.24%, and relative to our matched-budget One-Spike-style adaptation by 42.83%, 47.61%, and 34.03% on Cora, Chameleon, and Squirrel.
facts.model: matched-budget adaptations evaluated on frozen two-layer GCN checkpoints
facts.aggregation: three-seed mean per dataset and control
facts.uncertainty: descriptive paired comparison; no formal CI claimed
facts.measurement_scope: reported test split and matched-budget adaptations

facts.statement: Task superiority was not established: T=2/4 accuracy and teacher-agreement deltas were mixed across budgets, and the earlier task-superiority target failed. The accepted claim is bounded task degradation rather than universal task gain.
facts.model: frozen two-layer hidden-16 GCN checkpoint seeds 0/1/2
facts.uncertainty: negative evidence retained; no equivalence claim

internal.note: External process records and reviewer wording remain outside writer context. A²Q/One-Spike are matched-budget adaptations and require the later 36-reference audit before novelty language.
